what_its_for: Telmisartan is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It may also be used to lower the risk of heart attack or stroke in people who are at high risk for heart disease.
how_to_take: Take telmisartan by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not crush or chew the tablet.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 40 mg once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose to between 20 mg and 80 mg per day depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store telmisartan tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep tablets in their original blister packaging until you are ready to use them. Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using potassium supplements or salt substitutes that contain potassium unless your doctor tells you it is okay, as telmisartan can raise potassium levels. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and make you dizzy. Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without checking with your doctor, as they can reduce how well telmisartan works and may harm your kidneys. Do not take aliskiren (Tekturna) with telmisartan if you have diabetes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; feeling faint or very dizzy; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; signs of kidney problems such as little or no urination, swelling in your legs or feet; or if you become pregnant while taking this medication. Also contact your doctor if your blood pressure readings are not improving.
when_it_works: Telmisartan starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take 4 to 8 weeks of regular use before you feel its full blood pressure-lowering effect. Even if you feel fine, keep taking it every day — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, and stopping the medication can cause your blood pressure to go back up.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take telmisartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if telmisartan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may need a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may start you on a lower dose (20 mg). Use with caution if you have kidney problems. Children: This medicine is not recommended for use in children under 18 years of age.
